endorsements.quote: Addressing these biases requires that training datasets be representative of diverse patient groups and that models undergo continuous validation to ensure equitable outcomes.
To mitigate this risk, AI should be implemented as a complementary tool that augments, rather than replaces, clinical judgment[ 31 ].

Informed consent protocols should reflect the complexity of AI integration, ensuring that patients are not only aware of its benefits but also of potential limitations or areas where human oversight is critical[ 33 ].

unlisted_practices: Establish regulatory clinical guidelines and ethical standards that require explainability and accountability in AI algorithms.
Conduct robust validation studies of AI tools before integrating them into routine clinical practice.
Develop user-friendly interfaces for AI tools for healthcare providers.
Implement stringent data security measures and ensure compliance with data protection regulations such as GDPR.

screen.reason: This is a letter/commentary discussing ethical and clinical challenges (privacy, bias, human-in-the-loop) regarding AI deployment in wireless capsule endoscopy.
